terms.definition: A finite, unambiguous sequence of steps that transforms an input into an output — the core object of study in computer science.
A prefix tree: each edge consumes one character, so all words sharing a prefix share the path to it — the structure behind autocomplete.
A hash table mapping each word to the documents containing it — the same core structure full search engines are built on.
The pipeline stage that splits raw text into normalized tokens: punctuation stripped, lowercased, stop-words dropped.
A high-frequency word with little meaning on its own (the, is, of…) that indexing skips to save space.
A score ranking documents for a query; this engine uses term frequency — how often the words appear in the file.
A ~100 character window of the original text around a match, with the matched words highlighted for preview.
The cross-platform web server built into ASP.NET Core; it serves this app at http://localhost:5000.
A structure pairing keys with buckets via a hash function, giving average O(1) lookups — used for the inverted index itself.
Notation describing how an algorithm's cost grows with input size; the Trie's insert is O(length of word).
The body of documents an engine indexes; here, every .txt file inside the selected folder.
A measured timing; System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch wraps indexing and search so exact milliseconds reach the UI.
